texts: If you have a backup from when you were granularity 2, updating it from your new 3 will be hellish expensive because all the files have moved. Click the button here to granularise your backup, too, so it has the same folder structure as your client. Trust me, this will save lots of time.

THIS IS SERIOUSLY ONLY FOR ADVANCED USERS. THE MIGRATION IS BIG AND SLOW, SO USERS WITH >1m FILES SHOULD THINK CAREFULLY.

DO NOT DO THIS IF YOU DO SYMLINK MAGIC INSIDE YOUR FILE STORAGE

The client uses many subfolders to split up your collection into manageable chunks. As clients have grown, we are pushing from a granularity of 2, which means 512 subfolders, to 3, which means 8,192.

Migrating to a higher granularity requires running a job here and then repeating it on your backups.
Your granularity is currently 2. If you are an advanced user, you are invited to move to 3.

dialogs:
We are going to be rearranging your file storage completely. The process can be cancelled if it is taking too long, but it has to do the same amount of work to undo. If it fails half way through, I will attempt to undo it.

 Ideally, your client is currently calm and not trying to import many things. Granularisation migration works at about this speed:

NVME/SSD: 3,000-5,000 files/s
SATA/USB HDD: 100-500 files/s
NAS/SMB: 50-250 files/s
Cloud storage: should not be attempted
BTRFS and EXT4 filesystems may be up to 10x this speed.

If this is going to be too slow for you, it is ok to back out!

Do you have a recent backup, in case something goes wrong?
yes, I have a backup and I am ready
